## Deterministic graph evaluation

Build the CLI, then run the native MEX suite:

```bash
npm run build
npm run eval
```

`npm run eval` is equivalent to `npm run eval:graph -- --all` and creates an immutable timestamped
run under `.mex/eval-results/graph/`. This location is deliberate: graph scanning does not consult
`.gitignore`, while `.mex/**` is excluded by the scanner. The harness rejects an output directory
inside the subject if archived source there could contaminate the graph.

sources.docs/design/legacy-upgrade.md:
## Cleanup and recovery

The preview includes exact managed instruction-block replacements, obsolete
SETUP/SYNC removals, unchanged MEX-owned old skill files, disposable Wiki cache
hashes and any owned watch hook removal. Outside instruction bytes, BOM and line
endings stay intact. Modified/unowned skills, links, custom hook paths and
ambiguous hooks stay in place with a review finding. No recursive deletion runs.

The 0.8 watch installer never saved a hook backup and trimmed trailing whitespace
from a pre-existing hook. Those historical bytes cannot be reconstructed. Only
an exact, wholly generated released hook is removed automatically. Mixed or
edited hooks are preserved for manual review; upgrade never claims to have
restored an unavailable original.

The local journal records approved output before applying it. `mex upgrade
--finish` resumes interrupted local writes, worktree writes, commit or explicit
PR creation. `--discard` drops only owned pending tracked output; already-applied
personal/local changes stay. Edited output, unrelated files, links or changed
branch identity stop recovery/cleanup without forcing worktree removal. A
completed checkout receipt prevents repeating the import. Existing telemetry
opt-out remains untouched; successful interactive upgrade invokes the existing
versioned, once-only notice owner. JSON previews never display that notice.

This slice does not remove the old Wiki/setup engine, convert Inbox/Relay
records, qualify the three release repositories or publish a release.

sources.docs/design/model-budget.md:
## Callers and storage

`runModel` accepts `automatic: { estimate }`, with the four token classes. An
automatic caller must use a known reference-price model and an enabled project
or machine job. This flag records intent; running an automatic job from a
foreground worker does not exempt it. Existing setup calls remain explicit.
Later learning/filter job kinds must use this API; no such task is added here.

Migration 4 adds Node-owned `model_batches` and nullable `model_calls.batch_id`.
The ledger contains queue/owner IDs, requested model, mode, project/job/batch
attribution, timestamps, reservation/charge units, pricing metadata and state.
It contains no prompt, reply, credential or raw diagnostic. Observed model
labels remain independent of the requested model, including `unknown` when the
provider omits its label. The hooks schema remains version 1; Go recognizes
record version 4 without writing it. Older Node writers refuse the newer file.

The shared process owner acquires admission, launches one child, drains pipes,
records usage, reconciles and releases the lane. A database unique index allows
one running admission. Job context carries the writer's home through accounting
so a custom background record cannot accidentally use another CLI's home.

sources.docs/design/knowledge-entry-store.md:
## Trust and reads

Storage gates run on write and read. Hidden formatting/control characters are
stripped. Recognized Markdown and shell-command forms must be present in
repository CI runs, package scripts or documentation, or reference an existing
contained script. Unverified payload commands and HTTP links are removed while
the surrounding claim remains. Secret patterns and credential assignments,
including structured check values, are refused without echoing their contents.
Provenance references are distinct from payload links.

Only person or repository evidence qualifies a team entry. Person creation
requires its actual typed quote; repository sources must exist. Review evidence
requires two distinct PR source checks. Observed/mined/agent-memory hints cannot
be promoted by copying their metadata to the team directory. Reads recheck the
gates because a branch can edit entry files directly. Withheld entries are
reported as such. Unknown or redirected storage and incomplete bounded scans
fail closed. Secret-bearing old bytes are not included in previews.

Labels are derived: personal/person, team/evidence and hint/observation count.
Precedence is current request, personal notes, repository instructions, team
entries, hints. The store ranks its three entry levels accordingly. Current
requests and instruction-file delivery remain consumer responsibilities. Team
projections also report whether exact bytes are on the known default branch;
unknown default-branch state is never presented as shared.

sources.docs/design/knowledge-entry.md:
## File and fields

```markdown
---
mex:
  id: mx_7f3k2a
  kind: recipe
  scope: ["test/**"]
  source:
    type: person
    ref: mex note 2026-11-13
    quote: Tests use fixtures because fixed data makes failures reproducible.
  evidence: person
  one_line: Tests use fixtures because fixed data makes failures reproducible.
  checks: []
  status: active
  created: 2026-11-13
---
Tests use fixtures because fixed data makes failures reproducible.
```

`id` is `mx_` followed by at least six lowercase letters/digits. IDs are random,
stable, never reused, and match the filename. The implementation accepts up to
64 letters/digits and mints 24 hexadecimal digits.

Required fields are `id`, `kind`, `scope`, `source`, `evidence`, `one_line`,
`checks`, `status` and `created`. `kind` is recipe, rule, decision, pitfall,
procedure, fact or hint. Scope is one or more repository-relative globs; `**`
means the whole repository. Absolute paths and parent traversal are refused.

Source has a `type` (person, docs, review, ci, config, rule-file, mined,
observed or agent-memory) and a `ref` (a path, link or session reference).
A person source also needs its exact `quote`; a writer claiming a person
source must verify that quote against the supplied typed text. `mex note`
retains the text passed explicitly to the command, without model inference.
Evidence is person, docs, review, ci, mined or observed.

`one_line` is the complete claim in one line, never an automatic truncation.
`when` optionally contains `{type, match, pattern}` items: type is anti,
required, rejected or creates; match is literal or structural. Optional
`companions` are entry IDs. Unknown metadata is refused.

Status is active, proposed or retired. A proposed entry was written by an agent
and isn't in force yet: it is never delivered as accepted knowledge, never
written into a rule file, and can be read, retired or given aliases, but its
claim can't be edited. A retired entry keeps the same ID and file, with
`retired: {reason, by, at}`. `created` and `retired.at` are calendar dates, without
clock times. The body is an authored fact and reason, normally one or two
sentences. Structural validation does not judge the truth or wording of prose.

Verdicts, last-used values, delivery counts, and other per-checkout observations
never belong in this file. They belong in the local record. Legacy Wiki
metadata (`triggers`, `edges`, `last_updated`) is not accepted.

sources.docs/extractors.md:
## Language extractors

The frozen interface is [`src/graph/extraction/types.ts`](../src/graph/extraction/types.ts). The TypeScript implementation in [`src/graph/extraction/languages/typescript.ts`](../src/graph/extraction/languages/typescript.ts) is the reference implementation.

A `LanguageExtractor` must be:

- Pure and deterministic for the same tree, file path, and source.
- Limited to one parsed file: no filesystem, network, LLM, or cross-file lookups.
- Read-only with respect to the Tree-sitter tree.
- Complete for the language constructs claimed by its tests.
- Based on `generateNodeId(filePath, kind, name)` for stable node identity.

The engine owns parsing, grammar loading, body hashes, fingerprints, resolution, persistence, and timestamps. Do not implement those concerns inside an extractor.

sources.CONTRIBUTING.md:
## Code-graph contributions

The code graph ships in mex 0.7.0. For any code-graph issue, agree on a bounded, fixture-backed scope and create your branch from `main`:

```bash
git switch main
git pull
git switch -c <feature-or-fix-branch>
```

Open the pull request against `main`.

Changes to graph identity, reconciliation, schema, or drift semantics are core changes. Open an issue and agree on the approach before implementing them.

Language extractor and framework resolver contributors should read [Extending the code graph](docs/extractors.md) before starting. It documents the frozen interfaces, registration points, fixtures, tests, and required proof for a pull request.

sources.docs/design/legacy-upgrade-reader.md:
# Read-only 0.8 upgrade inputs

`src/upgrade/legacy-reader.ts` supplies `readLegacyScaffold(projectRoot)` for
the 0.8-to-0.9 migration. This first layer reads inputs only. It does not expose
a command, convert entries, delete caches, rewrite instructions or publish a
change. Those operations belong to the following upgrade stages.

The result preserves exact UTF-8 text (including BOM and CRLF), byte hashes,
source paths, canonical Wiki entities and their authored grounding baselines.
Root-level groundings without a file-level entity remain unattributed. Log
records retain their original fields and source lines. The reader never calls
an old verification timestamp a current check, and never supplies a new baseline.

It reads `.mex/config.json`, scaffold Markdown, root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`,
and `.mex/events/decisions.jsonl`. Configured Wiki exclusions remain excluded.
Team-owned Markdown, including Inbox proposals and Relays, is returned separately
for preservation, without interpreting it as knowledge. Local files, saved
diagrams, evaluation output and new learned entries are outside this reader.
Graph/Wiki databases and their sidecars are never opened, even for status checks.

Malformed metadata, duplicate identities, damaged log rows, unreadable sources,
redirected paths and safety limits produce bounded code/path diagnostics. Source
prose and raw filesystem errors do not enter those diagnostics. Readable material
remains available for inspection, but `complete: false` must block conversion.
Informational codec diagnostics do not make an otherwise complete read partial.
Unlike the index reader, upgrade refuses malformed root `grounds_to` values
instead of silently dropping their evidence from a complete observation.

Every read uses a regular-file descriptor, rejects links/junctions and parent
redirects, bounds allocation and total retained bytes, and rechecks file and
directory identities. A final verification rejects modifications, replacements,
directory additions and newly appearing optional inputs during the observation.
Directory contents are re-enumerated and compared under a separate bounded
verification budget because Windows can defer directory timestamp changes.
File reads also compare a second descriptor pass against the captured bytes,
and final verification rechecks source hashes under its own corpus bound. This
detects same-size edits when Windows defers file timestamps until handle close.
Consumers must still revalidate source hashes before applying a later preview;
this observation is not a durable lock on the user's files.
